title: Talu tenant API
description: The typed contract for a Talu tenant NAMESPACE — quota, RBAC, network baseline, security groups, dashboards and log gateway. Each VM is a separate talu-vm release with its own schema. Every property carries x-talu-owner: 'consumer' = the integrator writes it per tenant; 'operator' = the site supplies it once from environments/<site>/tenant-defaults.yaml (merged by the HelmRelease BEFORE spec.values). A consumer that sets an operator-owned field still wins the merge — the split is a contract, not an enforcement — but only the consumer-owned subset is API surface with a compatibility promise. See docs/architecture/adr-api-layer.md §4 and §10.1.

projectUuid.description: talu.io/project-uuid stamped on every object; the manager join key.

slug.description: Tenant namespace name; frozen at creation.

allowedUsers.description: Tenant members (emails) allowed to SSH and hold the scoped RBAC role.

resourceQuota.description: Optional ResourceQuota hard limits (e.g. requests.cpu, requests.memory).

internalIpPool.description: Tier-1 CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool CIDR (empty = off). Consumer-owned, but the CIDR must come from the site's IPAM plan — a consumer cannot invent one.

networkBaseline.description: Layer B opt-in: default-deny egress/ingress on tenant VMs except DNS + own ns + host/health.

securityGroups.description: Cloud-style allow-rules rendered to CiliumNetworkPolicies. Membership is declared BY THE VM (talu-vm renders a talu.io/sg.<name> label this policy selects on) — a VM is its own object since the split, so groups can no longer list VM names. Use allVMs to apply a group to every VM in the tenant.

allVMs.description: Apply to every VM in the tenant regardless of what the VMs declare (the old empty-vms behaviour).

dashboards.description: Per-tenant Perses dashboard + prom-label-proxy (reachable only via Pomerium); off by default.

logging.description: Tenant side of VM logging: Tier 2 renders this tenant's Cilium-pinned ingest gateway, which hard-stamps the namespace on lines the guests push. The guest side (consoleLevel/agent/paths) lives in talu-vm.

agent.description: Tier 2: run the in-guest agent + render the per-tenant ingest gateway.
